The department's activities are conducted at two main locations: Natrium on Medicinaregatan 7B in Gothenburg, and the Kristineberg Marine Research Station in Fiskebäckskil. The current position is located at the premises in Gothenburg, which is where Herbarium GB is situated. The latter hosts more than one million specimens from around the world (~60% imaged; ~28% with digitized metadata) and forms part of a global network of almost 4,000 herbaria.
Subject area 
Botany, specializing in vascular plant systematics.
Subject area description 
Vascular plant systematics is the scientific study of the diversity, evolutionary relationships, and taxonomy of vascular plants. In the 21st century, systematics is a highly integrative discipline, one that engages a diversity of data types and methodologies, and has strong connections to evolutionary biology, ecology, and conservation biology. For this position we seek a plant systematist having competence in the tools of modern systematics, a strong interest in natural history collections, and whose research makes first-hand use of material housed in such collections.
 
Duties 
This associate senior lectureship initially comprises 60% research and teaching in botany and 40% curation of the vascular plant collections at Herbarium GB. The curation component comprises contribution to strategic development of the collections, basic curation, and curation-related research.
Teaching and research tasks include:
Development of and engagement with a sustained, substantive, and productive research program focusing on vascular plants. A significant component of the research should be collections-based, making use of herbarium material.
Building and leading a research group, including applying for external research funding and publishing in high-quality scientific journals.
Teaching topics in plant taxonomy, systematics, and related subjects at undergraduate and graduate levels. This includes lecturing, coordination of practical exercises, course leadership, and project supervision.
Supervising doctoral students.
Participation in the development and renewal of teaching, in both content and form.
Development of collaborations with other research groups at University of Gothenburg and with researchers at other institutions. The department is especially keen to strengthen its collaboration with the Gothenburg Botanical Garden, with respect to research, teaching, and collection management.
Participation in and development of societal collaboration projects.

Curation tasks include:
Participation in the development of strategic goals and drafting of grant applications for Herbarium GB.
Curation and development of the vascular plant collections in Herbarium GB.
Execution and publication of research relating to or arising from curation activities.
Promoting integration of Herbarium GB into university- and botanic garden-based teaching, research, and community activities.
Support of digitization and database cataloguing in line with international standards for specimen data.
Support of visiting researchers and promoting collaboration with national and international institutions.

 
Eligibility 
Eligibility for employment as an associate senior lecturer is regulated by the Higher Education Ordinance and the University of Gothenburg's employment regulations.
To be eligible for appointment as an associate senior lecturer, the applicant must have been awarded a PhD or has the corresponding research expertise. Primary consideration should be given to a person who has been awarded a PhD or achieved the equivalent expertise within seven years of the deadline for application for employment as an associate senior lecturer. However, a person who has been awarded a PhD or achieved equivalent expertise at an earlier date may also be considered if there are exceptional circumstances. Exceptional circumstances are sick leave, parental leave, or other similar circumstances. 
Ability to teach in English is a requirement.
Assessment criteria 
The assessment criteria for appointment as associate senior lecturer are governed by the Higher Education Ordinance and the Appointments Procedure for Teachers at the University of Gothenburg. We seek candidates who have demonstrated the ability to independently initiate, develop, and conduct high-quality research within the subject area of the position. For appointment as an associate senior lecturer at the Faculty of Science and Technology, academic and teaching qualifications must be adequate in relation to the subject content and job description of the advertised position.
For this position, emphasis is placed on research qualifications and expertise, particularly in herbarium specimen-based research, with curation skills considered to be of similar importance. The assessment categories of collaboration with the wider community and management and administrative expertise are considered advantageous.
The assessment of research and curation skills includes
Proficiency in vascular plant systematics, taxonomy, and nomenclature, as evidenced by publications and participation in scientific conferences.
Experience of herbarium curation and/or collections-based taxonomic research.
Advanced knowledge of modern techniques in taxonomy and systematics, including phylogenetic and phylogenomic tools.
A clear vision of the future role and operation of herbaria, and thoughts on the priority actions required to realize that vision.
Experience of herbarium digitization, georeferencing, and/or database development.
Knowledge of the Northern Eurasian and/or Eurasian floras, specifically floristics and regional plant identification.

Personal qualities such as initiative, organization skills, pedagogical insight, and communication skills will also be taken into consideration..
Employment 
Type of employment: Fixed-term employment for five years
Extent: Full-time (100%)
Location: Gothenburg
Starting date: By agreement

The School of Medical Sciences at Örebro University is seeking a postdoctoral researcher in Biomedicine (Molecular Virology and mRNA Vaccine Development) for a fixed-term appointment.
Subject area
The subject area for this position is Biomedicine.
Background
The School of Medical Sciences at Örebro University is seeking a postdoctoral researcher to join the Cellular and Molecular Virology research group.
The position is part of the research project "Development of novel mRNA-based TBE vaccines", funded by the Knowledge Foundation (KK-stiftelsen). The project focuses on the development and evaluation of novel mRNA-based vaccines against tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV).
The research builds on extensive expertise in the molecular biology of tick-borne flaviviruses, viral reverse genetics, virus–host interactions and vaccine development. The project is conducted in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners.
Duties and responsibilities
The appointment as a postdoctoral researcher is intended to enable persons who have recently been awarded their doctoral degree to consolidate and further develop their research skills.
The successful candidate will conduct experimental research focusing on the molecular biology of tick-borne flaviviruses and the development of novel mRNA-based vaccines against tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV).
The work will include molecular cloning, viral reverse genetics, infectious cDNA clones, site-directed mutagenesis, and the generation and characterization of recombinant flaviviruses. Particular emphasis will be placed on investigating viral replication, virus–host interactions, and the molecular determinants of viral pathogenicity.
The researcher will also contribute to the design and evaluation of vaccine candidates using cell-based assays, in vivo animal models, neutralization assays, and relevant immunological methods. The project will be conducted in close collaboration with other researchers and industrial partners. The position also involves analysis of experimental data, preparation of scientific publications, and presentation of research findings.
Qualifications
To be eligible for appointment as a postdoctoral researcher, applicants must hold a doctoral degree, or an equivalent foreign degree, in a subject relevant to the position, such as molecular virology, virology, molecular biology or biomedicine.
Applicants who are in the final stages of their doctoral studies and expect to complete their PhD before the employment decision are also encouraged to apply. The doctoral degree must be completed no later than the time of the employment decision.
Priority will be given to applicants who have obtained their doctoral degree no more than three years before the application deadline, in accordance with the applicable postdoctoral employment agreement. Exceptions may apply under special circumstances.
The applicant may not previously have held a position as a postdoctoral researcher for more than one year in the same subject and at the same higher education institution. The position is for a term of at least 2 years initially but may be extended for a further 1 year. If the person during the period of employment has been on parental leave, the period of employment is to be extended by the corresponding number of days. The period of employment may also be extended in the event of absence due to illness.
Assessment criteria
To see the job advertisement in its entirety, visit https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/job/?jid=20260286.
Information
The position is a full-time (100%) fixed-term appointment for two years, preferably starting in January 2027. The appointment may be extended for up to one additional year, if required to fulfil the purpose of the appointment, subject to available funding and applicable regulations. Salary is determined individually based on qualifications and experience.
For further information about the position, please contact Professor Magnus Johansson, School of Medical Sciences, Örebro University, e-mail: magnus.johansson@oru.se.
At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.
Örebro University actively pursues equal opportunities and gender equality as well as a work environment characterised by openness, trust and respect. We value the qualities that diversity adds to our operations.
Application
Applications are submitted online via Örebro University's recruitment system.
A complete application should include the following documents:
A cover letter, describing your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation for applying for the position.
A curriculum vitae (CV), including relevant research experience, scientific publications, and contact details for at least two references.
A description of scientific qualifications and research achievements.
Copies of relevant degree certificates or, for applicants who have not yet completed their doctoral degree, documentation confirming the expected date of completion.
Relevant scientific publications (maximum of ten, submitted in full text).

Only documents written in Swedish, English, Norwegian or Danish can be considered.
For more information about the application process, please visit Örebro University's website: https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/
The application deadline is November 19, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!
We decline any contact with advertisers or recruitment agencies in the recruitment process.
As directed by the National Archives of Sweden (Riksarkivet), Örebro University is required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

At Westermo, we develop and manufacture industrial data communication solutions used in critical infrastructure worldwide. As an Electronics Engineer, you will be part of our Hardware Department, developing the robust, high-quality products that have made Westermo a trusted global supplier.

Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or similar

Experience in electronics hardware design

Fluent in English, both written and spoken

Meritorious

Experience developing industrial products or products used in demanding environments

Are you a business-minded research professional with deep expertise in medical imaging who thrives in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment?
Do you enjoy combining scientific and technical expertise with commercial understanding, taking ownership and driving complex research collaborations towards successful outcomes?
Collective Minds is looking for a Director, Research Programs & Consortia to drive our portfolio of public and private research collaborations. This is a broad, hands-on role with significant responsibility and the opportunity to make a real impact in a growing international healthtech company.
About Collective Minds
Collective Minds is based in Stockholm/Danderyd and we operate globally across clinical trials and life sciences. We are an imaging platform for clinical trials that connects hospitals, experts, and industry - including CROs, pharma, biotech, medtech, and eClinical vendors - enabling trials with imaging endpoints and the generation of high-quality evidence faster and more efficiently. We are a fast-moving, commercially minded team focused on collaboration, accountability, and impact. By combining deep domain expertise in medical imaging with novel cloud technology, we help customers reduce risk, ensure compliance, accelerate and scale research.
About the role
As Director, Research Programs & Consortia, you will take responsibility for our portfolio of more than 10 public and private research consortia, which are a key part of Collective Minds' strategy and ongoing delivery.
Working alongside CROs, biotech and medtech companies, pharmaceutical partners, academic hospitals and research organizations, these collaborations span medical imaging, big data, analytics, and AI modeling and validation across therapeutic areas such as oncology, immunology, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal research.
Within these projects, Collective Minds acts as a data manager and platform provider, bringing deep expertise in medical imaging to support complex research collaborations.
You will be responsible for successful project delivery, reporting and project close-outs, while coordinating project and research managers across our customer delivery organization. You will act as a playing coach andpersonally manage selected research consortia and contribute scientific and technical expertise when needed.
This is a broad, hands-on role where you will combine scientific expertise with commercial understanding, set priorities and drive results through collaboration. You will ensure projects are delivered efficiently, within agreed scope and with a clear focus on quality and business value.
Your main responsibilities:
Drive the research project portfolio, ensuring successful delivery within agreed budgets, timelines, scope and commitments.
Coordinate project and research managers, aligning priorities, following up on progress and ensuring accountability across projects.
Personally manage selected research consortia, including scientific, technical and operational activities.
Provide scientific and technical guidance across medical imaging, data analytics, AI modeling and validation.

Manage budgets, project scope and stakeholder expectations, balancing scientific objectives with commercial priorities.
Ensure accurate reporting to customers, funders and partners, including grant deliverables and efficient project close-outs.
Collaborate with clinical and technical operations teams to plan capacity, resolve challenges and continuously improve project delivery.

Who are we looking for?
We are looking for a scientifically experienced and business-minded professional who combines deep expertise in medical imaging with a strong track record of delivering complex research projects.
You are analytical, pragmatic and comfortable working independently in a fast-moving environment. You enjoy collaborating across disciplines, making decisions and finding effective solutions without adding unnecessary complexity.
You communicate clearly, build trust with internal and external stakeholders and know how to balance scientific quality with business priorities and efficient execution.
We believe you have:
A strong scientific background in life sciences, medical sciences, biomedical engineering or a related field, with deep expertise in medical imaging research.
Experience from a commercial life sciences, medtech, biotech, pharma, CRO or healthtech environment, including scientific and academic collaborations.
Proven experience managing complex research programs or consortia, including budgets, timelines, scope, reporting and project close-outs.
Hands-on experience with research consortia, work package delivery, grant writing, grant execution and funding-related reporting.
Strong technical skills, including scientific programming, analytical tools and data-driven research workflows.
The ability to assess complex scientific and technical requirements, make informed decisions and contribute to technical implementations when needed.
Commercial awareness and the ability to balance scientific objectives with budgets, resources and project commitments.
Strong communication, coordination and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to drive results across teams and external partners.
A proactive, hands-on and solution-oriented approach, with the ability to adapt quickly and take initiative.
Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
Willingness to travel internationally as required by research projects, typically approximately every two months.
Ability to work regularly from our Stockholm/Danderyd office.

Why join Collective Minds?
At Collective Minds, you will join an innovative and ambitious company where technology, science and collaboration come together to make a meaningful difference in healthcare.
You will be part of an entrepreneurial environment with short decision-making processes, engaged colleagues and the opportunity to influence how things are done.
This is an opportunity to take responsibility for a strategically important research portfolio, work with leading scientific and industry partners and contribute to the continued growth of an international healthtech company.
We look forward to receiving your application!

Required Qualifications
Master's degree in Microbiology, Biotechnology, Life Sciences or a related scientific discipline, or equivalent experience.
5-8 years of experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device or another highly regulated industry.
Strong experience in Quality Control Microbiology or a related quality function.
Proven knowledge of GMP requirements and microbiological quality systems.
Experience leading investigations, deviation management and change control activities.
Experience conducting risk assessments and applying Quality Risk Management principles.
Experience supporting audits, inspections and regulatory compliance activities.
Ability to communicate scientific concepts clearly and professionally to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Professional proficiency in Swedish and English, both written and spoken.

 
Preferred Experience

Experience representing QC in cross-functional projects and improvement initiatives.
Experience coaching, mentoring or providing technical guidance to colleagues and stakeholders.
Knowledge of Lean, Yellow Belt methodologies or other structured continuous improvement tools.

Department of Forest Ecology and Management  
Scientific background
Atmospheric aerosols are microscopic particles that influence weather and climate, contribute to biogeochemical cycling, and facilitate the dispersal of organisms. Aquatic systems can release aerosols into the atmosphere through processes such as bubble bursting, which have been studied extensively in oceans. However, whether and how these processes operate in streams remains poorly understood.
Streams differ from oceans in their hydrodynamics and water chemistry, potentially affecting how particles are captured by bubbles and potentially transferred to the atmosphere. Recent observations suggest that streams contain ice-nucleating particles that could become airborne, raising the possibility that boreal streams represent an overlooked source of atmospheric aerosols. The magnitude of these emissions, the mechanisms driving them, and the environmental factors controlling them remain largely unknown
About the position  
The postdoctoral researcher will investigate the hypothesis that streams emit aerosols to the atmosphere and identify the mechanisms and environmental conditions governing these emissions. A central task will be to develop a flux chamber to capture aerosols emitted from stream surfaces and quantify aerosol fluxes using online particle counters and air filtration for laboratory measurements of ice-nucleating particles. The chamber is planned to be deployed in both controlled experiments and field studies in natural boreal streams. The job also includes water sampling and measurements of physicochemical water and bubble properties.
The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to experimental design, data collection and analysis, manuscript preparation, scientific publication, and other forms of research communication. The position will be supervised by Associate Professor Marcus Klaus.
The successful candidate will be expected to work independently while collaborating closely with other members of the research team and external partners. The research environment will provide opportunities to develop scientific expertise, establish collaborations, and strengthen the candidate's professional development and academic career prospects.
Your profile
We are seeking a motivated and dedicated researcher with expertise at the interface of aquatic and atmospheric sciences and a strong interest in air–water exchange processes. Applicants must hold a PhD in atmospheric sciences, aquatic sciences, physics, environmental engineering, or a related discipline. 
The applicant must have demonstrated experience in measurements of aerosols, suspended particles and/or air-water mass exchange (particles or gases) and experience conducting laboratory and/or fieldwork in aquatic and/or atmospheric systems. A track record of scientific writing and publishing in peer-reviewed journals is also required, as are excellent written and spoken English skills.  
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:
Air filtration, aerosol sampling, and particle counting
Droplet freezing assays
Bubble and/or turbulence characterization
Programming and data analysis using tools such as R or MATLAB
Engineering, instrument development, or practical skills relevant to designing and constructing the flux chamber  

In addition to scientific qualifications, emphasis will be placed on personal suitability, including scientific curiosity, initiative, the ability to work independently, and a constructive and collaborative approach to teamwork. 
As postdoctoral appointments are career-developing positions for junior researchers, we are primarily looking for candidates with a doctoral degree that is three years old at most.
